column20: What went wrong and why? — 'A recent change to Allocator behavior ... had been progressively rolled out over the prior two months'
column21: What happened? — 'an issue with the Allocator service in the Azure Compute control plane'
column22: What went wrong and why? — 'an Allocator service deployed per Availability Zone' in East US 2
column23: What happened? — 'two Availability Zones (physical AZ02 and AZ03) in the East US 2 region'
column24: What went wrong and why? — 'Customer deployments failing in AZ03 were automatically redirected to AZ02' ... 'led to overload and throttling in AZ02'
column25: How did we respond? — 'We stopped all new VM deployments in AZ02' and backlog draining continued until 19:30 UTC
column26: What went wrong and why? — 'ARM depends on several VM management services in the Azure control plane' whose Allocator throttling caused the impact
column27: How can customers make incidents like this less impactful? — 'multi-region geodiversity strategy to avoid impact from incidents like this one that impacted a single region'
column28: Trigger is a behavior change staged over two months; AZ03-to-AZ02 auto-redirection cascaded into a zone-wide backlog with manual throttling and slow drain to full recovery
